why: D-616 measured U1's ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 ANTENNA KEEP-OUT naming four copper layers where its own master names *.Cu, declared it an OPEN FABRICATION BLOCKER, and refused to close it without a route in hand.  This is that route -- and the same clamp turns out to hold FOUR MORE keep-outs this board owns at board level, which no check here had ever looked at.

detours.why: Three In3.Cu segments of the charge-input rail between the through via at (66.450,102.300) and the junction at (45.750,139.350).  All three cross the ANTENNA region: the first clips its north-west corner between y=104.000 and y=104.36, and the dogleg apex at (64.700,120.450) sits 0.200 mm inside the west boundary.  VBUS_CHG class, so it stays on In3.Cu at its own 0.500 mm width with no barrel.

A SECOND, SEPARATE chain of the same net, and it exists because BOSS1_KEEPOUT was clamped to four layers too: the 9.334 mm segment (45.750,139.350)-(39.150,132.750) crosses that mounting boss's In3.Cu face diagonally, which nothing on this board had ever been able to ask.  Detoured LOCALLY, to the through via at (36.800,135.100), so the +3V3 In3.Cu pocket that bonds R20.1 through the via at (43.100,131.400) is left where it is.
detours.max_mm_why: 12.657 mm of copper that must now walk round a 4.500 mm square keep-out whose south-east corner (43.250,133.750) sits 1.131 mm off the straight line it used to take.  13.500 mm is 0.843 mm of headroom over the original, 6.7 %, and is stated here rather than assumed: the other two chains come away SHORTER than the copper they replace and are held to that.

detours.why: A 110.000 mm signal trunk on the +3V3 In3.Cu plane, 40.350 mm of it lying WHOLLY inside the antenna region at x=66.350.  Both chain ends are F.Cu-B.Cu through vias of this net -- (66.350,103.650) and (19.900,120.800) -- so the run may terminate on any layer those barrels span; it is given In2.Cu.  Its own In3.Cu slot is priced by clause K6 and must SHRINK.

licences.why: U1's FOOTPRINT-EMBEDDED ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 antenna keep-out.  Its MASTER writes `*.Cu`; the board's copy named four layers, which is the whole of KiCad's `lib_footprint_mismatch` on this board (62 of 62 pads are identical).  330 mm2 of the region is on-board and In3.Cu/In4.Cu held 273.697 / 304.259 mm2 of pour and five track segments.

The BOARD-LEVEL DUPLICATE of the same antenna region, same outline, its own uuid, `footprints allowed`.  `pcbnew.BOARD.Zones()` does not return a footprint's zones and a footprint's does not return the board's, which is why D-616's screen -- which reads footprint zones -- never saw this one, and why nothing else on this board saw U1's.

M2 mounting-boss retention point, 4.5 mm keep-out (38.75,133.75)-(43.25,138.25).  20.250 mm2 on board; In3.Cu held 8.983 mm2 of +3V3 plane and In4.Cu 14.561 mm2 of GND pour under a moulded boss, with NO tracks and NO vias -- a free carve.
The second M2 mounting boss, (57.75,0.75)-(62.25,5.25).  20.250 mm2 on board; In3.Cu 14.508 mm2 and In4.Cu 14.508 mm2 of pour, no tracks, no vias.
MK1's acoustic port, (3.0,96.0)-(5.0,98.0).  4.000 mm2; In3.Cu and In4.Cu held 2.105 mm2 of pour each, no tracks, no vias.
